items.text: The Q2 travel and expense summary shows that rail costs rose 14% against the previous quarter, largely because of the regional fare increases announced in March. Hotel spend stayed flat, while client entertainment dropped slightly after the new pre-approval rule took effect. Finance reminds all staff that receipts must be uploaded within five working days of travel; the automated tool that flags missing receipts only runs on Mondays, so late uploads can delay reimbursement. Managers should review their team's open claims before the 15 July cut-off.
Meeting note: the phone upgrade for the field sales team has been pushed to September because handset stock is still short.
Expense claim EC-2291 was rejected on 4 June because the taxi receipt was a photograph of a screen rather than the original PDF.

Notes from the operations review, 12 June, Metroline Rail Services.

Present: H. Okafor (chair), T. Lindqvist, R. Patel, S. Byrne.

1. Train strike contingency. The RMT strike on 22-24 June will remove roughly 60% of services on the northern corridor. HR confirmed that staff who cannot reach their usual site may work from the Bristol office or from home without a formal change of contract. Line managers should keep a written record of who was affected.

2. Phone upgrade. The device refresh for client-facing roles is now paused pending the new procurement framework. Anyone whose handset is out of warranty should raise a ticket with IT; temporary loan units are available from the fourth floor store.

3. Expense claim backlog. Finance reported 112 claims older than 30 days. Patel noted that the approval chatbot introduced in April is still being tuned and has been misreading multi-currency receipts, so all claims above £500 are being checked manually until further notice. The chatbot is a topic here, not a decision-maker; final approval stays with the cost-centre manager.

4. Actions:

| Action | Owner | Due |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Circulate strike travel guidance | Okafor | 17 June |
| Confirm loan handset stock | Byrne | 19 June |
| Audit claims over 30 days | Patel | 26 June |

The travel policy sets out how employees should handle disruption during industrial action. If a planned journey cannot be made because of a train strike, staff may claim a refund of the unused ticket and, where a replacement journey was necessary, the cost of reasonable alternative transport. Claims must be supported by the cancellation notice and a short explanation. Policy owner: People Operations, last reviewed February.
Train strike update: the 07:42 and 08:10 services from Reading are cancelled on Thursday; passengers should use the replacement bus from the north car park.

When you submit an expense claim for a missed or disrupted journey, attach the train operator's cancellation email and, if you booked a replacement, the new ticket. The system will route anything over £250 to your director automatically. Claims submitted without supporting documents are returned to the claimant rather than rejected outright, so you can add the missing file and resubmit. Please do not open duplicate claims for the same journey; if you have already submitted one, email expenses@northfieldgroup.co.uk with the claim reference.

A recent survey of 400 staff found that most people learned about the June train strike through the internal newsletter rather than the intranet. The same survey showed that only a third had used the new expense chatbot, and those who did generally found it quicker than the old web form. Several respondents said they would like the phone upgrade scheme to include a buy-out option for personal devices.

Specification: Expense Claim Intake Service (v0.9)

Purpose. The service accepts claim submissions from the employee portal, validates required fields, and forwards complete claims to the approval queue. It does not approve or pay claims.

Input example:

```json
{
  "claim_ref": "EC-2291",
  "employee_id": "U-4482",
  "category": "rail",
  "amount_gbp": 86.40,
  "receipt_attached": true,
  "travel_date": "2025-06-05"
}
```

Validation rules. A claim is complete when claim_ref, employee_id, category and amount_gbp are present and receipt_attached is true or the category is "mileage". Claims that fail validation are returned with a reason code (E01 missing field, E02 receipt required, E03 amount exceeds category limit).

Notes for the team. The intake service was never intended to replace the approval chatbot used by Finance; the two are separate systems and share only the employee ID. Errors in the chatbot's receipt matching should be raised with the vendor, not patched here. Unit tests cover the three reason codes plus the mileage exemption; integration tests against the staging queue run nightly at 02:00.
Phone upgrade window: eligible staff can order their replacement handset from 1 August using the IT self-service page.
